header.running_head: Pledging Allegiance to the Injunctions of Islaam

blocks.text: A narration of Bayhaqi adds that everyone from the youngsters to the elders as well as men and women all pledged their allegiance to Islaam and to the Shahaadah at the hands of Rasulullaah ﷺ.[^2]
Hadhrat Mujaashi (RA) and his Brother (RA) pledge allegiance to Islaam and Jihaad

Hadhrat Mujaashi bin Mas'ood (RA) narrates that he and his brother went to Rasulullaah ﷺ and he said, "Accept our pledge of allegiance to Hijrah." Rasulullaah ﷺ said to them, "Hijrah (to Madinah) has finished with those who have already made Hijrah (the compulsion to migrate to Madinah no longer exists)." When Hadhrat Mujaashi (RA) asked what was it that he could pledge his allegiance to, Rasulullaah ﷺ replied, "Pledge your allegiance to Islaam and to Jihaad."[^3]
Hadhrat Jareer bin Abdillaah pledges allegiance to Islaam

Hadhrat Ziyaad bin Ilaaqa narrates that when Hadhrat Mughiera bin Shu'ba (RA) passed away, he heard Hadhrat Jareer bin Abdillaah (RA) address the people saying, "I advise you to fear the One Allaah Who has no partner and to remain graceful and calm. With these hands of mine did I pledge allegiance to Islaam at the hands of Rasulullaah ﷺ and he stipulated that I always remain a well-wisher for every Muslim. I swear by the Rabb of the Kabah that I wish well for each one of you." He then sought forgiveness from Allaah and descended from the pulpit.[^4]

Bayhaqi and others have narrated from Hadhrat Ziyaad bin Haarith Sudaa'ee (RA) that he approached Rasulullaah ﷺ and pledged allegiance to Islaam. The rest of the Hadith has already been mentioned in the Chapter of Da'wah.[^5]
